entities.title: Result envelope (UtvResult)
entities.summary: Every JSON-layer operation answers a UtvResult, and UtvResult::to_json writes it as a utv-result/1.0 object with schema, operation, status, diagnostics and candidates.
consumers: Callers of the JSON layer, and the shared fixture runner tests/everyday.rs, which compares status, candidates, operation and diagnostic codes
The typed layer, which turns a UtvResult into an Outcome and back (Outcome::to_result)
guarantees: operation is the everyday contract name (parseIso, formatIso, fields, add, compare, daysBetween, posixSecondsBetween, contains, overlaps, resolve, toZone, toOffset, parseText, formatText), validate for the validators, convert for native conversions and from_json, construct for a typed constructor's refusal.
status is one of the Status values written in kebab case: invalid, unsupported, indeterminate, none, unique, multiple, range, symbolic, resource-limit, error, valid.
unique has exactly one candidate and multiple all of them, ascending; none, invalid, unsupported, symbolic and validation results have none.

Each diagnostic is {code, severity (error, warning, info), path, message}; codes are the shared ones of docs/library-api.md section 5, plus the validator's envelope.* and structural.schema details after malformed-value.
entities.compatibility: The JSON layer is kept unchanged in behaviour (README, The JSON layer). The fields a full utv-result/1.0 has beyond these (cardinality, manifest, assumptions, loss) are not emitted; see the limitation no-result-manifest.

relationships.description: In part: the mandatory fields beyond operation, status, candidates and diagnostics are missing.
